commands.name: install
commands.description: Install dependencies exactly as the lockfile pins them, across the workspaces.

commands.name: build
commands.description: `tsc -b` across the workspaces, then each package's postbuild. This is where typechecking happens — there is deliberately no separate `typecheck` script to keep one answer to 'do the types hold'. It is the first gate because `verify` runs it first and the suite reads built output.

commands.name: test
commands.description: The suite, via the package script rather than a bare `vitest run`, so the runner is whatever the repo says it is.

commands.name: lint
commands.description: ESLint. Blocking because a worker can fix it by editing its own output, which is the line between a gate that teaches and one that nags.

commands.name: pregate
commands.description: The local antagonistic review panel, run against the working tree's diff from main via scripts/verified-pregate.mjs — an in-repo wrapper that verifies the sibling script's pinned digest before invoking it, so it can carry the credentials below safely. ADVISORY: it reports findings and blocks nothing, so a REJECT is a conversation and not a verdict. It COSTS REAL MONEY on every run — several model calls per lens — which is why it is a release step named one at a time rather than a gate that fires on every verification. This row's 40-minute timeoutMs is the OUTERMOST of three nested timeouts — see AGENTS.md § Operating this repo for the full derivation (why 3 + 8 + 16 = 27 minutes, and why each layer must fire before the next) rather than restating it here. It is deliberately ABOVE scripts/verified-pregate.mjs's own 35-minute spawn bound, which is deliberately ABOVE the panel's own hardcoded 30-minute inner backstop (PREGATE_TIMEOUT_MS default): the innermost backstop fires first so a run can report which lens hung, and this row's timeoutMs exists only to catch a wedge neither inner layer caught.
